newsitem.title: ITALY: Bad luck strikes again in Italian lottery fiasco.
newsitem.headline: Bad luck strikes again in Italian lottery fiasco.

text.p: Italy's New Year lottery, branded a fiasco after a winning number was dumped because of a technical hitch, ran into more problems on Saturday after officials ruled that the person eventually awarded the prize could not have it.

The consumers' association Codacons, which campaigned for the whole draw to be scrapped and repeated, scored a victory on Friday when the Council of State, the highest administrative court, upheld its petition for the fifth prize win to be suspended.

Top prizes in Italy's biggest lottery were drawn live on television on January 6 but the state games committee ruled the next day that the number that won the two billion lire ($1.25 million) fifth prize was invalid because the draw machine stuck.
Only six of the 10 numbered balls dropped into one of the draw machines from which the seven-digit combination was selected.
When the problem came to light, the games committee awarded the prize instead to the person whose number was the first one drawn after the six main prizes had been selected.
But the Council of State decided that the switch was unfair and the "new" fifth prize winner should stick with his or her original 200 million lire win.
"We made our decision because of the delicacy of the issue," Aldo Pezzana, who presided over the ruling, said.
The fifth prize money has been frozen for the time being.
The unprecedented foul-up in what is traditionally a prestigious draw has scandalised lottery-loving Italians.
"The lottery is destined to be redone, if not totally then at least in part," Codacons chairman Carlo Rienzi said.
"I advise everyone to hang on to the tickets they bought."
The Treasury is holding an inquiry into the affair and has yet to publish the winners' names officially. Commentators say the matter could take months to clear up.
